elements.element: The liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Subsection (b) applies the aggregate cap to “EACH PARTY'S” liability.

elements.element: The fee-based limb of the cap includes fees paid or payable.
elements.evidence: The fee limb expressly includes “FEES PAID OR PAYABLE BY LICENSEE.”

elements.element: The fee-based limb measures the 12 months immediately preceding the claim.
elements.evidence: The clause measures the period preceding “THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM,” not the 12 months preceding the claim. Those triggers can produce different periods.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of the applicable 12-month fee amount and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Subsection (b) expressly uses the greater of the stated fee limb and USD 1,000,000.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect damages is mutual.
elements.evidence: Subsection (a) states that neither party is liable to the other for indirect damages.

elements.element: The exclusion of consequential damages is mutual.
elements.evidence: Subsection (a) states that neither party is liable to the other for consequential damages.

elements.element: Each party's breach of confidentiality obligations is carved out from the cap on an uncapped basis.
elements.evidence: Confidentiality breaches are named as Excluded Claims and excepted from the cap, but the retained “UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCE SHALL LICENSOR BE LIABLE” language independently covers technology-use claims alleging violation of contractual or common-law rights and is not clearly subject to the Excluded Claims exception. The carve-out is therefore not fully effective against Licensor.

elements.element: Each party's breach of data protection obligations is carved out from the cap on an uncapped basis.
elements.evidence: Data protection breaches are named as Excluded Claims, but the retained absolute Licensor immunity can independently bar technology-use claims alleging violation of statutory or other rights. The text does not clearly apply the Excluded Claims exception to that immunity.

elements.element: Each party's breach of security obligations is carved out from the cap on an uncapped basis.
elements.evidence: Security breaches are named as Excluded Claims, but the retained absolute Licensor immunity can independently bar overlapping technology-use claims alleging violation of contractual, statutory, common-law or other rights.

elements.element: Each party's indemnification obligations are carved out from the cap on an uncapped basis.
elements.evidence: Indemnification obligations are named as Excluded Claims, but the retained sentence categorically disclaims Licensor liability for claims that use of the technology results in infringement or other rights violations. That can defeat claims under Licensor's corresponding indemnification obligations.

elements.element: Each party's gross negligence is carved out from the cap on an uncapped basis.
elements.evidence: Gross negligence is named as an Excluded Claim, but the retained “UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCE” Licensor immunity is not qualified by culpability and can bar overlapping claims even when based on gross negligence.

elements.element: Each party's wilful misconduct is carved out from the cap on an uncapped basis.
elements.evidence: Wilful misconduct is named as an Excluded Claim, but the retained absolute Licensor immunity is not expressly made inapplicable to wilful misconduct and can bar overlapping rights-violation claims.

elements.element: Each party's fraud is carved out from the cap on an uncapped basis.
elements.evidence: Fraud is named as an Excluded Claim, but the retained absolute Licensor immunity is not expressly subject to that exception and can bar overlapping rights-violation claims.

elements.element: Each party's infringement of the other party's intellectual property is carved out from the cap on an uncapped basis.
elements.evidence: Although infringement of the other party's IP is named as an Excluded Claim, the retained language states that “UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCE SHALL LICENSOR BE LIABLE” for claims that use of the technology results in infringement of any person's IP. This directly undermines the carve-out as to Licensor.

elements.element: Customer's payment obligations do not constitute damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: The final sentence excludes only Licensee's obligation to pay “FEES DUE.” It does not cover all Customer payment obligations, such as other contractual reimbursements or amounts payable.

elements.element: The liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Subsection (b) applies the aggregate cap to “EACH PARTY'S” liability.

elements.element: The cap amount is 12 months' fees.
elements.evidence: The cap is the greater of the 12-month fee amount and USD 1,000,000, so it is not limited to 12 months' fees.

elements.element: Each party's indemnification obligations are carved out from the cap on an uncapped basis.
elements.evidence: Indemnification obligations are named as Excluded Claims, but the retained absolute Licensor immunity can defeat overlapping indemnification claims, particularly claims concerning technology-related infringement.

elements.element: Each party's breach of confidentiality obligations is carved out from the cap on an uncapped basis.
elements.evidence: Confidentiality breaches are named as Excluded Claims, but the retained absolute Licensor immunity can still bar overlapping claims alleging violation of contractual or common-law rights.

elements.element: Each party's gross negligence is carved out from the cap on an uncapped basis.
elements.evidence: Gross negligence is named as an Excluded Claim, but the retained “UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCE” Licensor immunity is not qualified by culpability and is not clearly subject to the exception.

elements.element: Each party's wilful misconduct is carved out from the cap on an uncapped basis.
elements.evidence: Wilful misconduct is named as an Excluded Claim, but the retained absolute Licensor immunity can still bar overlapping claims and is not clearly overridden.

result.reason: The redline adds the intended mutual cap structure and named Excluded Claims, but it uses the event giving rise to the claim rather than the claim as the lookback trigger, excludes only fees due rather than all Customer payment obligations, and leaves a sweeping one-sided Licensor immunity that conflicts with the purported carve-outs—most directly for IP infringement. The fallback also fails because the cap can exceed 12 months' fees. Stale Licensor-specific wording, a run-on structure and the unresolved contradiction materially reduce drafting quality.
